questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Real-Time Data Streams”?
options: Real-Time Data Streams helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Real-Time Data Streams means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Real-Time Data Streams removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Real-Time Data Streams should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Real-Time Data Streams helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Real-Time Data Streams is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “WebSocket stream fundamentals” in this lesson?
options: Treat “WebSocket stream fundamentals” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “WebSocket stream fundamentals” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “WebSocket stream fundamentals” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “WebSocket stream fundamentals” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “WebSocket stream fundamentals” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “WebSocket stream fundamentals” under Real-Time Data Streams. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Real-Time Data Streams”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
